A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same formula-harvesting, UMAPS and Conservative Matrix Field research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated proofs and renumbered formula tables.

before.justification: V2 reports original formula-harvesting and unification outcomes, LLM equivalence tests and extractor comparisons in Sections 4–5 and Tables 2–4.

after.justification: V3 retains original computational and LLM results and adds hyperparameter sensitivity experiments in Appendix D and generated-formula analysis in Section 5.4.

M1.justification: The reported canonicalization pipeline adds numerical validation and Maple MinimalRecurrence after RISC fitting. The code-repair prompt also expands the supplied error excerpt from 50 to 400 characters (v2 F.6.3; v3 I.6.3). The core clustering, folding and UMAPS procedure remains; rational-function fitting was already present in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 455,050-paper corpus, subject categories, target constants and CMF trajectory/start-point ranges. V3's convergence summary and sensitivity experiments retain this coverage. Lower formula/source counts change the retained sample, without establishing a new domain or task.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview for equivalence testing, and GPT-4o, Claude 3.7 Sonnet and GPT-4o mini as extractors. The new sensitivity study varies the existing algorithm's parameters and clustering control.

E3.justification: V3 adds a substantial evaluation design: clustering-granularity and threshold sweeps with a no-clustering control, UMAPS depths from 4 to 120, and Guess depths from 8 to 500 over 100 random formulas. Appendix D normalizes runtimes to default settings, while Section 5.4 introduces trajectory-normalized convergence r/ℓ1(t). These are added protocols; the retained benchmark settings do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests whether clustering loses recoverable links, how UMAPS fitting depth affects recovery and runtime, and whether Guess recurrences generalize across fitting depths. V3 also adds false-positive examples in I.4–I.5 and CMF metric scans in G.6. V2 lacks these systematic sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the benchmarks. V3's random formula samples and numerical substitutions concern validation design, not repeated-run uncertainty. Its checklist adds no concrete statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 4 changes related formulas from 381/407 to 360/385 and CMF-embedded formulas from 188/407 to 166/385; source papers decrease from 154 to 140. Canonical counts, long formula-table entries and LLM scores remain unchanged. V3 adds sensitivity/runtime results and a 1,693-formula CMF summary, including 57 with reported normalized convergence 1.76. Revised totals with different denominators do not establish a same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: V3 adds the N ≥ 2d + 1 recovery corollary and proof, conditional projective uniqueness, a Poincaré–Perron limit lemma, and extensive hypergeometric/CMF convergence derivations (C.3.1, E.3, F.2 and G). It also corrects the worked certificate's pA from 12n−7 to 12n−17 (v2 A.1.1; v3 B.1.1). Existing necessary-condition proofs are retained in F.1.

C1.justification: The central symbolic-unification contribution remains. The abstract revises its quantitative totals, and the introduction adds qualified novelty claims concerning the first LLM–symbolic-tool integration for number-theory discovery and possibly the first integration with a proprietary research-grade computer algebra system.

C2.justification: V3 explains runtime tradeoffs in the sensitivity results and why trajectory normalization removes artificial convergence acceleration from folding. It adds an interpretation of unrecovered high-degree coboundaries and an outlook involving higher-dimensional CMFs and D-finite constants. The original LLM and manual-substitution limitations are largely retained and reorganized.

D1.justification: V3 documents exact rational fitting through SymPy, 30 random recurrence checks with tolerance 10^-10, Maple minimality checking and the cluster used for sensitivity experiments. Appendix J adds filenames and detailed schemas for two supplemental pickle datasets, including formula provenance. The repository and interactive-demonstration links are unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 expands discussion of symbolic regression and LLM–tool integration, citing PAL, ToRA, Parsel and program-search research. It adds mathematical context concerning minimal recurrences, discrete flat connections and D-finite CMFs. These additions refine the positioning while retaining the central symbolic-unification research agenda.

P1.justification: V3 adds a glossary and NeurIPS checklist, separates Limitations from Outlook, and relocates existing coboundary proofs into a dedicated appendix. The introduction and several explanations are edited, but most existing narrative and technical exposition remain recognizable and substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: V3 adds a substantial set of displays: four sensitivity tables (7–10) and two CMF metric visualizations (Figures 7–8). Figure 5 is enlarged to full width, and main-text floats and the formula-source table are reflowed. The long canonical-form tables retain their entries and basic design.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens justification and verification of the central pipeline. Appendix D supplies sensitivity evidence absent from v2, showing that the chosen clustering preserves maximal observed linkage while reducing runtime against no clustering. Additional conditional theory, recurrence validation/minimality checks, a corrected worked certificate and dataset schemas improve auditability. These gains outweigh remaining reporting defects, notably I.5's inconsistent statement that removing 147 candidates from 660 leaves 535.
